target.title: fix(sweep): allow PR review lease comments
target.body:
# Summary

- Grants the scheduled review shard's target App token `pull-requests: write`, while retaining its existing `issues: write` scope.
- Adds a focused workflow regression test that requires both write permissions in the `Create target review token` block.

# Problem

The scheduled ClawHub sweep in [run 29261805316](https://github.com/openclaw/clawsweeper/actions/runs/29261805316) minted a token with `issues: write` but `pull-requests: read`. Review-shard lease/status comments use `POST /repos/{target}/issues/{number}/comments`; on PR items that endpoint needs the App's Pull requests write permission. All 29 ClawHub PR shards therefore received `403 Resource not accessible by integration`, while the one ordinary issue succeeded.

This is independent of [PR #518](https://github.com/openclaw/clawsweeper/pull/518)'s recovery/fanout handling and [PR #521](https://github.com/openclaw/clawsweeper/pull/521)'s ledger lifecycle work.

# Implementation

Only the review-shard `Create target review token` block in `.github/workflows/sweep.yml` changes:

- `permission-pull-requests: read` becomes `permission-pull-requests: write`.
- No recovery, queue, state publication, labels, gates, application credentials, or other token scopes change.

# Validation

- `pnpm run build:all` — passed.
- `node --test --test-name-pattern "sweep target review token can post pull request review leases" test/sweep-workflow.test.ts` — passed (1/1).
- `node --test --test-name-pattern "sweep target review token can post pull request review leases|review workflow gives Codex a read-only inspection token" test/sweep-workflow.test.ts` — passed (2/2).
- `node --test --test-name-pattern "codex subprocess env strips GitHub and App credentials|codex subprocess env can expose an explicit read-only GitHub token" test/clawsweeper.test.ts` — passed (2/2).
- `node --test test/sweep-workflow.test.ts` — passed (62/62) in Linux local-container Crabbox proof, provider `local-container`, lease `cbx_8c70bf6e5438`, commit `f38ac5bb6d75f01ea21fdf2d70927b0965dedde4`. The one-shot lease stopped automatically.
- `pnpm exec oxlint test/sweep-workflow.test.ts --deny-warnings` — passed.
- YAML parse of `.github/workflows/sweep.yml` — passed.
- `git diff --check origin/main...HEAD` — passed.
- `actionlint` — unavailable on this host: executable is not on `PATH`.
- `pnpm run format:check` reports pre-existing formatting differences across 373 files, including both unchanged full files touched here; no repository-wide formatting rewrite was applied.

# Credential-boundary proof

- The review shard still receives the short-lived target review token as `GH_TOKEN` only for deterministic review orchestration and lease/status publication.
- A distinct `Create target Codex inspection token` step requests only `contents: read`, `issues: read`, and `pull-requests: read`. The `Review shard` step passes that token separately as `CLAWSWEEPER_PROOF_INSPECTION_TOKEN`.
- `src/codex-env.ts` deletes inherited `GH_TOKEN`, `GITHUB_TOKEN`, App credentials, and `CLAWSWEEPER_PROOF_INSPECTION_TOKEN` before reinjecting only the explicit inspection token for the Codex subprocess. Existing tests cover both stripping inherited credentials and passing an explicit inspection token.

This preserves the intended boundary: deterministic workflow code can post the lease/status comment; the untrusted Codex subprocess receives the separate read-only inspection credential.

# Deployment prerequisite and installation evidence

The ClawSweeper GitHub App installation for `openclaw/clawhub` must allow **Pull requests: Read & write**. `actions/create-github-app-token` can narrow an installation permission but cannot grant a permission that the installation does not have.

The installation settings endpoint is not readable with the available user authentication: `GET /repos/openclaw/clawhub/installation` returns `401 A JSON web token could not be decoded`. The capability is nevertheless proven by redacted live workflow evidence from the failing parent run itself: [run 29261805316](https://github.com/openclaw/clawsweeper/actions/runs/29261805316), job `Publish review artifacts` ([86858453103](https://github.com/openclaw/clawsweeper/actions/runs/29261805316/job/86858453103)), ran `Create target write token` at 2026-07-13T15:27:35Z for `openclaw/clawhub` with `permission-pull-requests: write`; that step succeeded and its normal post-step cleanup revoked the token. The pinned workflow at the run head requested the same write scope. This establishes that the installation could mint a ClawHub PR-write token at incident time; the remaining defect was that the review shard requested only PR read.

# Post-merge behavior proof

The requested real App-token proof cannot be produced from this unmerged branch: scheduled review shards execute the default-branch workflow, and this PR does not dispatch or rerun workflows. Before treating the rollout as complete, a maintainer must:

1. Let a normal scheduled or maintainer-requested review process one ClawHub PR and one ordinary issue after this change is deployed.
2. Capture redacted run output and the two resulting lease/status comment URLs, then request `@clawsweeper re-review`.

# Risks and rollout

The additional scope is limited to the short-lived review token already used for deterministic lease/status comments. Repository contents, checks, statuses, and the Codex inspection token remain read-only. The remaining proof is a post-deployment normal-run observation; this PR does not dispatch or rerun anything.

# Codex review closeout

- `codex review --uncommitted` — clean; no accepted or actionable findings.
- `codex review --base origin/main` — clean; no accepted or actionable findings.

target.title: fix(local-review): use selected Codex CLI
target.body:
## Summary

Use the operator-selected Codex CLI for local-only reviews and the matching local preflight.

## Problem

`review --local-only` injected `CLAWSWEEPER_PREFER_WINDOWS_CODEX_APP=1`, forcing the Windows Desktop app binary at `%LOCALAPPDATA%\OpenAI\Codex\bin\codex.exe`. On the reported host that binary is stale and rejects the requested model, while the user's normal `PATH` Codex CLI works. The local preflight selected the same Desktop binary, which could validate a different executable than the review runner.

## Implementation

- Stop injecting the Desktop-app preference for local-only reviews.
- Make `pnpm run codex:local:check` use the same normal `CODEX_BIN`/PATH resolution.
- Preserve explicit `CODEX_BIN` precedence.
- Document PATH-based local-only selection and add Windows-oriented launcher regression coverage.

Production `.github/actions/setup-codex` remains separate and pinned at `@openai/codex` `0.139.0`; this PR does not modify it.

## Validation

- `node --test test/codex-process.test.ts test/command.test.ts test/clawsweeper.test.ts` — passed (88 tests).
- `pnpm run lint:scripts` — passed.
- `pnpm run build:all` — passed.
- Focused `oxfmt --check` for changed source, script, and test files — passed.
- `git diff --check` — passed.
- `pnpm run check` ran build and lint successfully, then hit unrelated native-Windows prerequisite failures in existing unit tests: WSL `/bin/bash` unavailable for Bash-helper tests, Windows symlink permission failures, and `npm.cmd` `EINVAL` in runtime packaging. This PR does not broaden into test-harness or platform-policy changes.

Proof boundary: native Windows local launcher selection only; no workflow or CI-matrix changes.

## Codex review closeout

- `codex review --uncommitted`: initially found that the preflight still selected a different executable; accepted and fixed that P1.
- Final `codex review --uncommitted`: clean, with no accepted/actionable findings.
- `codex review --base origin/main`: clean, with no accepted/actionable findings.
- Empty commit `c8899b5554` refreshed PR checks without changing source files; `git diff --check` and a second `codex review --base origin/main` remained clean.

## Risks and rollout

Local-only review and preflight now use the first spawnable `codex` command on `PATH` unless the operator sets `CODEX_BIN` explicitly. No local CLI is pinned or updated. Production setup remains unchanged. This branch is independent of #539.

target.title: feat(dashboard): group OpenClaw Bay terminal pools
target.body:
## Summary

- Consolidate the rare terminal outcomes into one **Failed / cancelled** attention pool.
- Give **Completed** the larger terminal shoreline: up to 20 individual outcomes at standard desktop width, while constrained widths keep 12 labels readable and make the remaining `+8` explicit.
- Replace the unclear timing badge with **Avg end-to-end …** or **Awaiting a timed run**.

## Problem

OpenClaw Bay used three similarly sized terminal pools even though completed outcomes are the common case. This left useful completion space unused while making the terminal shoreline visually fragmented. The top-right timing badge also displayed values such as `15s` without saying what was being measured.

## Implementation

- Keep the existing `completed`, `failed`, and `cancelled` terminal records and sweep target compatibility, but render failed and cancelled together in an attention pool with their individual outcome styling preserved.
- Increase completed-pool layout capacity to four columns / 20 visible outcomes on a standard desktop terminal stack. At narrower widths, keep labels legible with a 12-item limit and an explicit overflow note instead of shrinking them excessively.
- Rename the badge to **Last hour · Avg end-to-end …**. It uses the existing `total_duration_ms` for recent completed ClawSweeper jobs: workflow run start-to-completion, not a per-lane wait time.

The UI deliberately says **job** rather than promising an exact per-reference average: a fan-out job can cover more than one GitHub item. In the usual exact-review flow, a job normally maps to one item.

## Validation

- `pnpm run build:dashboard`
- `node --test test/dashboard-worker.test.ts` — 93 passed.
- `pnpm run lint:dashboard`
- `pnpm exec oxfmt --check dashboard/bay-page.ts test/dashboard-worker.test.ts docs/proof/openclaw-bay/run-proof.mjs docs/proof/openclaw-bay/README.md`
- `git diff --check`
- Deterministic browser proof on Crabbox local-container (`cbx_a397c065e00e`, `swift-shrimp`, Playwright `v1.60.0-noble`): 25 assertions passed, including distinct terminal groups, 20 visible completed items at desktop width, 12 readable items plus `+8` at constrained width, and a generated real tide that washes 20 outcomes. Browser direct GitHub API requests: 0. Mutation requests: 0.
- `codex review --uncommitted` — clean after proof-artifact refresh.
- `codex review --base origin/main` — clean; terminal-pool consolidation and refreshed proof artifacts are internally consistent.

## Proof

- [Proof README](docs/proof/openclaw-bay/README.md), [storyboard](docs/proof/openclaw-bay/playwright-proof-storyboard.jpg), [trace](docs/proof/openclaw-bay/trace.zip), and [assertion summary](docs/proof/openclaw-bay/proof-summary.json) are checked in.
- The proof exercises the real local `/bay-demo` route and replaces only `/api/status` with a synthetic redacted fixture. It contains no credentials, cookies, authorization headers, local Windows user paths, or live private payloads.

## Risks and rollout

- Presentation-only: no worker/data-schema/API contract change and no added GitHub endpoint, request, or refresh work.
- On narrow screens the completed pool intentionally shows an explicit overflow rather than overlapping labels; wide screens use the new 20-outcome capacity.

target.title: fix(sweep): bound failed shard recovery
target.body:
## Summary

Makes failed review-shard recovery durable and one-shot. A recovery now waits for an acknowledged exact-review queue write instead of treating a GitHub event delivery as proof that a replacement review run exists.

## Problem

The failed-shard recovery job could send a `repository_dispatch` event and accept GitHub's HTTP acknowledgement as success. The later legacy router could then create repeated replacement `workflow_dispatch` runs for stale open items after the originating worker had finished. That bypassed the durable queue/lease decision at the point where failure was detected.

This was not author activity. For example, a scheduled sweep selected a large ClawHub set and its recovery fanned out directly:

- Parent scheduled run: [Review ClawSweeper items #29261805316](https://github.com/openclaw/clawsweeper/actions/runs/29261805316), created 2026-07-13 15:20:23 UTC; it selected 30 ClawHub shards and failed.
- Recovery run: [Review event items #29263452346](https://github.com/openclaw/clawsweeper/actions/runs/29263452346), created 2026-07-13 15:43:49 UTC and completed 15:56:22 UTC; it directly fanned out 29 ClawHub items, including `#2411`, `#2460`, `#2487`, `#2489`, `#2490`, `#2873`, `#2898`, `#2947`, `#2948`, `#2949`, `#2950`, `#2951`, `#2953`, `#2957`, `#2958`, `#2959`, `#2963`, `#2964`, `#2969`, `#2986`, `#3005`, `#3006`, `#3023`, `#3036`, `#3037`, `#3038`, `#3050`, `#3055`, and `#3056`.
- Earlier examples show the same pre-fix pattern: [#29249741130](https://github.com/openclaw/clawsweeper/actions/runs/29249741130) (34-item batch), [#29253817069](https://github.com/openclaw/clawsweeper/actions/runs/29253817069) (34-item batch), and [#29257701833](https://github.com/openclaw/clawsweeper/actions/runs/29257701833) (36-item batch).

The same mechanism explains the observed stale OpenClaw direct-review churn, including [openclaw/openclaw#67967](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/67967), [#92328](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/92328), and [#84975](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/84975). These are recovery fan-outs, not fresh review requests.

Separately, a live exact-review action-ledger publish on this PR's review run failed after eight non-fast-forward retries: [run #29262649242](https://github.com/openclaw/clawsweeper/actions/runs/29262649242) / [job #86859694467](https://github.com/openclaw/clawsweeper/actions/runs/29262649242/job/86859694467). That shared-state write contention is a distinct control-plane issue and is being investigated separately; this PR does not claim to solve it.

## Implementation

- Replace the failed-shard `repository_dispatch` hop with a signed POST directly to the existing durable `/internal/exact-review/enqueue` endpoint.
- Require a positive queue acknowledgement: queued, deduplicated, or explicitly disabled. A missing or invalid acknowledgement remains a failed recovery and is retried at most three times; it cannot be silently treated as delivered.
- Reduce the recovery job permissions to `actions: read` and `contents: read`.
- Preserve the target branch, make recovery review-only, and suppress verdict routing so recovery cannot close the target item.
- Enforce the queue invariant: a failed-shard recovery may create one item, but can never supersede pending, dispatching, or leased ordinary work or an active recovery. Expired leases are reclaimed before this decision, allowing a new recovery only when no live work remains.
- Add queue and workflow assertions for direct durable enqueue, acknowledgement handling, disabled-target handling, and active/expired lease behavior.

## Required operational follow-up

Re-authorize the `openclaw-clawsweeper` GitHub App installation for `openclaw/openclaw` with **Issues: Read and write** and **Pull requests: Read and write**. That configuration change is required to restore its intended comment, label, and close operations; it is not representable in repository source.

## Validation

- `git diff --check origin/main...HEAD`
- `pnpm exec oxfmt --check .github/workflows/sweep.yml dashboard/worker.ts src/repair/publish-event-result.ts test/clawsweeper.test.ts test/dashboard-worker.test.ts test/sweep-workflow.test.ts`
- `node --test test/dashboard-worker.test.ts` — 99 passed.
- `node --test --test-name-pattern="sweep review recovery uses explicit failed shard artifacts|failed review recovery waits for durable exact-review queue acknowledgement" test/clawsweeper.test.ts test/sweep-workflow.test.ts` — 2 passed.
- `pnpm run build:dashboard`, `pnpm run build:all`, and `pnpm run lint` — passed.
- The changed workflow `run:` block passed `bash -n` in `bash:5.2` Docker, using LF-preserved input.
- Docker `actionlint` reported only pre-existing main-branch diagnostics outside this change (lines 241, 528, 825, 2157, and 3426); it reported no diagnostic for the changed recovery block.

The broader native-Windows test attempt reaches Linux-hosted Bash helper tests through the machine's `docker-desktop` WSL distribution, which has no `/bin/bash`. That is an intentionally Linux-hosted surface, not a regression or a platform change in this PR; the affected workflow block was syntax-checked in Linux Docker instead.

## Live proof boundary

The linked ClawHub runs are pre-fix production evidence. Creating an artificial failed shard to demonstrate post-fix behavior would itself create control-plane load and would require a prohibited manual workflow dispatch. After merge/deploy, the safe confirmation is a naturally occurring failed review shard: it must produce one signed durable queue acknowledgement (or an explicit failed recovery), never a direct `workflow_dispatch` fan-out, and it must not replace live ordinary work.

## Codex review closeout

- `codex review --uncommitted` — initial findings on active recovery replacement, expired recovery leases, queue-delivery acknowledgement, and disabled-target acknowledgement were accepted and fixed; final dirty review clean.
- `codex review --base origin/main` — clean; no accepted/actionable findings.

## Rollout and risk

This changes recovery scheduling only; fresh review requests retain normal queue/retry behavior. The workflow uses the existing `CLAWSWEEPER_WEBHOOK_SECRET`, and touching `.github/workflows/sweep.yml` carries the normal GitHub OAuth/workflow scope risk. Deploy, then observe a natural failed shard as described above. The separate state-branch serialization problem remains out of scope for this PR.
